verdict_text:
NO

The `matrix_re` pattern only matches `attention.query_key_value.weight`, `mlp.dense_h_to_4h.weight`, and `mlp.dense_4h_to_h.weight` per layer — it omits `attention.dense.weight`, so only 48 tensors (3 per layer × 16) are cast to bfloat16 instead of the required 64 (4 per layer × 16), violating clause 1. The `attention.dense.weight` tensors are consequently left in float32, so the output is missing 16 of the intended bfloat16 casts. Notably, the assertion `sum(...) == 48` matches this bug rather than catching it, so the required check "exactly 64 tensors are bfloat16" (per the Required checks section) is not actually enforced — the script asserts the wrong number and would pass despite violating the spec. This also means the "expected total 196 tensors" count may be right but the dtype distribution among them is wrong.
expected_defect: One projection family is missing from the bfloat16 cast pattern (the attention output projection stays float32); the artifact's own count check was adjusted to the wrong number.
note: experimenter: set `detected` (true if the stated problem matches expected_defect; for a correct artifact, true means a false alarm).
